condition_specific: cancer caused by exposure to IARC Group 1 or 2A carcinogens
filing_deadline_notes: Presumption does not apply if more than 20 years since last assigned to hazardous duty
notes: Rebuttable if: (1) outside-duty tobacco/high-risk exposure was probably a significant factor; (2) no IARC 1/2A carcinogen exposure shown; (3) cancer preexisted employment; (4) firefighter is age 70 or older. Applies to hazardous duty firefighters only. 'Hazardous duty' defined per 5 C.F.R. 550.902. Lookback period: presumption does not apply if more than 15 years (180 months) have passed since last assigned to hazardous duty (per HB 27, eff. September 29, 2017; prior data incorrectly showed 20 years).

condition_specific: cardiovascular disease caused by cumulative exposure to heat, smoke, toxic gases, chemical fumes and other toxic substances
filing_deadline_notes: Compensation payable only if disability/death results within 8 years after last injurious exposure (8-year limit does not apply to exposures occurring after January 1, 1976)
notes: Covers paid and volunteer firefighters. Applies to exposures after January 1, 1967. Requires prior injurious exposure in Ohio employment. Requires referral to qualified medical specialist before award. Compensation only for temp total, perm total, or death.

condition_specific: post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), without an accompanying physical injury
statute_citation: Ohio Rev. Code § 4123.01/§ 4123.87 (WC compensability pathway); § 126.65 (State Post-Traumatic Stress Fund)
notes: Two mechanisms were created together by H.B. 308 (133rd General Assembly, effective April 12, 2021): (1) a true workers' compensation pathway that amends the definition of "injury" (R.C. § 4123.01) so PTSD arising out of employment is compensable through the ordinary Bureau of Workers' Compensation claims process without an accompanying physical injury, removing Ohio's "mental-mental bar" for this occupational group (R.C. § 4123.87); and (2) a standalone State Post-Traumatic Stress Fund (R.C. § 126.65), a separate benefit fund covering "public safety officers" (paid and volunteer peace officers, paid and volunteer firefighters of a lawfully constituted fire department, and certified first responders/EMTs) for lost wages and medical, therapy, and hospital costs. The § 126.65 fund was left unfunded and administratively inoperative for nearly 5 years. H.B. 479 (136th General Assembly, the "Kandice Straub First Responder PTSI Support Act," signed June 24, 2026) created a First Responder PTSI Fund Commission within the Department of Behavioral Health to write claims-processing rules and administer the fund, and appropriated $40 million for FY2027. As of August 2026, claims-processing rules had not yet been fully finalized, so the fund may not yet be usable in practice even though it exists on paper. Applies to full-time firefighters.
